purpose: Canonical clean-room visual target for SLOPOS-I classic shell composition and styling.
source_note: Derived from the user-provided late-1990s platinum desktop screenshot with third-party branding, proprietary artwork, and non-goal elements removed or replaced.
must_have: thin dark keylines and classic raised/sunken control treatment
right-aligned desktop objects with Trash near the bottom-right
blue desktop background with strong contrast against platinum windows
coherent styling across first-party shell, settings, utilities, and representative upstream applications
must_not_have: Aqua-style glass, traffic-light controls, or modern macOS visual language
GNOME/libadwaita-style cards or oversized touch spacing
large rounded cards, pill controls, or pervasive rounded corners
third-party logos, product names, proprietary fonts, proprietary icons, or copied wallpapers
invented visual requirements not present in AGENTS.md or this manifest

required_scenes.description: Idle composed desktop with top menu bar, desktop objects, wallpaper, and no dock.
System/file-browser window in dense icon view with classic chrome.
Control Panels / Settings surface using the same compact classic visual language.
Compact About This Computer-style first-party information window using SLOPOS branding only.
Small utility such as Calculator or Notes proving compact utility-window styling.

critical_failures: bottom dock or Application Strip visible
settings or file-browser surface visually breaks from the classic shell language
direct use of third-party branding or proprietary visual assets
visual parity claimed without current screenshot evidence and a vision review
review_rules: Compare only against AGENTS.md and this reference manifest.
If a goal is not explicit or directly observable in the canonical reference, mark it UNKNOWN rather than inventing a requirement.
Report observable geometry, spacing, chrome, typography, icon-density, and composition differences instead of subjective aesthetic claims.
Missing evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
A critical failure forces FAIL regardless of numeric score.
Visual QA is evidence for appearance only; it does not prove packaging, architecture support, hardware support, or functional correctness.
